ruling: Stage 1 (by ~2026-11-01): a governor/legislature invokes emergency or moratorium authority against a named deployment; Stage 2 (by 2026-11-12/15): a named lab pauses or reverses that deployment, with the live dispute being whether the announcement follows Stage 1 and cites the state action (ai-pressure) or precedes it and cites public sentiment only (lab-moves revised, ai-public-backlash); Stage 3 (by 2026-11-15): no party other than the lab holds a cost-imposing hook over reversal, so whatever posture results stays reversible at will (ai-regulation-teeth revised).
because: Four minutes converge on a lab pause/reversal landing in the 6-8 week window, but ai-public-backlash and lab-moves-revised are mutually exclusive on ORDER (state-first vs. lab-first) and ai-pressure vs. lab-moves-revised are mutually exclusive on CITED REASON (state opposition vs. public sentiment alone). ai-regulation-teeth's round-2 revision reframes the decisive question away from 'which move happens' to 'does anything binding attach to it,' and explicitly survives only if no governor's order lands with a violation-consequence -- which is exactly what ai-public-backlash's Stage 1 would supply if it fires.
threat_live: Binding opposition immediately triggers moves to un-bind it: ai-pressure's lab lobbies for federal preemption the moment it makes a voluntary concession, and ai-regulation-teeth argues no third party gets a cost-imposing hook regardless of which move happens -- so accountability's appearance (a pause, a safety board) arrives newly live at this stage without enforcement attached, which is a more dangerous state than either open defiance or a real rule, since it forecloses stricter follow-through while reading as responsiveness.
strongest_minute: ai-regulation-teeth (round 2 REVISE) -- it is the only minute that names a falsifiable discriminator (does a party other than the lab hold a cost if the lab reverts) rather than predicting which theatrical form the response takes, and it explicitly stakes itself against ai-public-backlash's moratorium scenario rather than ignoring it.
weakest_minute: pressure-model -- its claim resolves true under either 'doubles down publicly before 2026-11-12' or 'faces a second, larger reversal,' with the second branch given no date or size threshold, so the prediction cannot lose within the stated window.
shared_assumption: ai-pressure, lab-moves, ai-incident-severity, and pressure-model all assume the visible response to binding opposition takes the form of a single named lab's deployment pause/reversal by ~2026-11-12/15, without arguing why a deployment-level move (rather than, say, a pricing, access, or geographic change) is the mechanism binding opposition acts through.
smuggled_assumption: ai-incident-severity requires a SECOND, unrelated firm to make a comparable reversal within 60 days to classify the event as structural -- the brief grants only that opposition becomes binding once, not that it recurs across firms, so the second-mover condition is an assumption the minute introduces rather than one the brief supplies.
unresolved: Whether the lab's move or the state's move comes first, and whether the lab's stated reason is state/local political opposition or undifferentiated public sentiment -- the minutes split on both and none of the visible evidence in round 2 settles either ordering.
